newsitem.title: USA: Occidental Petroleum meets with Colombian Indian leader.
newsitem.headline: Occidental Petroleum meets with Colombian Indian leader.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp, met Tuesday with a leader of a Colombian Indian tribe which has threatened mass suicide over oil exploration on their land, a company spokesman said.
At the meeting, tribal leader Roberto Cobaria invited executives to attend negotiations in Colombia later this month which aim to prevent the 5,000 members of the U'wa tribe from killing themselves.
The meeting took place at Occidental's headquarters here.
At stake are oil-rich lands that could boost profits for both Occidental and Colombia, which has seen production in other fields decline.
"The purpose of the meeting ...was to hear first hand his concerns," said an Occidental spokesman, referring to Cobaria.
"It wasn't intended as a negotiating session," he said.
The heads of Occidental's gas and oil exploration unit and its Colombian subsidiary attended the meeting.
Cobaria, in an earlier interview with Reuters, said his tribe did not want Occidental to extract oil, calling the substance "blood of the Mother Earth."
"If you let (Occidental) take out a little, they're there until there's no more, so better nothing," Cobaria said.
The Occidental spokesman said some issues would still have to be resolved.
Occidental has not decided whether to attend the meeting in Colombia.
"It's not a particularly safe area for outsiders," the Occidental spokesman said, noting that guerrillas, not tribal members, presented a security threat.
The Colombian government in March ruled that Occidental could begin exploring the land, but the company has delayed starting.
Occidental is the largest oil producer in Colombia, pumping 180,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude from the Cano Limon field.
